title: Networking tools
subtitle: Reachability, path, DNS, sockets, whois, packets — flip for meaning and notes

cards.meaning: Send ICMP echo requests — is the host reachable?
cards.notes: Runs until Ctrl-C. No reply ≠ always down — firewalls often drop ICMP.
-c = count. Useful in scripts so ping does not hang forever.

cards.meaning: Show hop-by-hop path toward a host
cards.notes: Map of the road, not just destination alive. Each router that answers is a hop.

cards.meaning: Similar path discovery; often works without root
cards.notes: Same idea as traceroute with fewer privilege needs on many systems.

cards.meaning: Short DNS lookup: name → IP or reverse IP → name
cards.notes: host = short answer. Contrast with dig for the full DNS packet.

cards.meaning: DNS lookup with full answer (question, answer, extra)
cards.notes: dig = full packet view. Use when host’s one-liners are not enough.
-x = reverse. Same job as host IP or nslookup IP.

cards.meaning: Query DNS; shows your resolver (#53) and A or reverse result
cards.notes: Server line is your resolver from resolv.conf. Non-authoritative = cached/recursive answer.

cards.meaning: Reverse DNS namespace — IP octets reversed under this domain
cards.notes: How nslookup/dig reverse lookups are structured. One IP can have several names.

cards.meaning: All TCP sockets, numeric addresses (no reverse DNS)
cards.notes: -a all, -n numeric, -t TCP. Look for LISTEN vs ESTABLISHED. Modern equivalent: ss.

cards.meaning: Listening TCP sockets plus PID/program name
cards.notes: -l listening, -p process. Root needed to see other users’ processes. Who owns the port?

cards.meaning: LISTEN = server waiting; ESTABLISHED = session up
cards.notes: Local address:port then remote. Bound to 127.0.0.1 = local only.

cards.meaning: Look up registrar/NIC records (owner, dates, contacts)
cards.notes: Answers “who owns this domain?” — not “what IP is it?” (that is DNS).
Needs privilege for most interfaces. Start with -i, then add host/port filters.

cards.meaning: Filter by IP or port; -w writes raw pcap
cards.notes: -w is for Wireshark later, not text. host matches source or destination.

cards.meaning: Boolean packet filter; quotes keep and/or for tcpdump
cards.notes: Without quotes the shell eats and/or. Parentheses group OR inside AND.
